verdict.rationale: HeyGen has no native rules engine in the evidence. Its pricing page lists first-party integrations with n8n, Make, HubSpot and Zapier, which let users wire event-triggered rules to HeyGen actions, though the rules themselves are defined in those external tools. Batch APIs with webhooks supply event signals but are only developer building blocks. Missing for 10: a native in-product rule/trigger builder, documentation of which events and actions the integrations expose, and hands-on corroboration of event-driven automation.
